bib.title: Harness-of-Harness: Multi-Day Autonomous Software Development with Continual Improvement

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Harness-of-Harness: Multi-Day Autonomous Software Development with Continual Improvement". Yan, Su, Zhang, Li, Zhang, Zhang, Chen, Bai, Hu (Shanghai AI Laboratory). Preprint, arXiv:2609.01481v1, 1 Sep 2026.

COVERAGE: All 53 pages and all 134,042 characters, including the supplementary appendices A–D. I read the reference list only as far as needed for the origins.

CORE CLAIM
HoH wraps an unchanged coding-agent harness in repeated Planner, Developer and QA Tester loops. Two things carry from one loop to the next: the artifact state (the code) and the evidence state (QA findings). Gains over a single pass are attributed to that carry-over.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
- **GameCraft-Bench** (45 of 140 tasks, stratified, seed 20260707), Overall score on a 0–100 scale. HoH@3 against Vanilla:

| Harness and model | Vanilla | HoH@3 |
|---|---|---|
| Codex + GPT-5.5 (high) | 49.58 | 71.52 |
| OpenCode + DeepSeek-V4-Pro | 26.90 | 48.98 |
| Pi + MiniMax-M3 | 42.16 | 58.78 |

- **FrontierSWE** (15 of 17 tasks), mean reward, Vanilla to HoH@3: Codex 0.31 to 0.54, OpenCode 0.23 to 0.31, Pi 0.26 to 0.55.
- **ProgramBench**, average test pass rate, Vanilla to HoH@3: Codex 60.41 to 66.50, OpenCode 45.27 to 57.56, Pi 35.83 to 52.68.
- **Ten loops** (Codex, FrontierSWE, 15 tasks): dominance goes from 39.33% at HoH@3 to 72.67% at HoH@10, peaking at 76.00% at HoH@9. Vanilla scores 27.33% in the same 11-checkpoint pool (p.12).
- **Case study "Fusepoint"** (a Godot first-person shooter, Codex with GPT-5.6-Sol): 70 loops over about 6 days. Of 81 recorded issues, 65 were closed and 16 were left open. 17 issues were reopened after a later change broke verified behaviour (p.15).
- **Run design:** every task-condition score comes from one valid run (Table 7, p.30). Failed infrastructure attempts were replaced, and no seeds or temperature were controlled.

ABLATIONS (Codex + GPT-5.5, GameCraft-Bench, 45 tasks, T=3, one run each; Table 3, p.14)
- **Budget control (Table 2):** each extra Vanilla pass was a "Continue developing and testing the current game" prompt in the same session. The table below gives scores and tokens per task.

| Passes | Vanilla Continuation | HoH |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 49.58 (2.59M tokens) | 59.71 (2.88M) |
| 2 | 54.99 (4.56M) | 64.84 (5.67M) |
| 3 | 58.24 (6.33M) | 71.52 (8.41M) |

- **Component removal:** each cross-loop channel was removed in turn. Scores are against full HoH@3 at 71.52.

| Variant | Score | Change | Tokens per task |
|---|---|---|---|
| w/o Plan Update | 63.39 | −8.13 | 7.56M |
| w/o Evidence Feedback | 65.23 | −6.28 | 7.46M |
| w/o Warm-Start (rebuild from empty each loop) | 63.67 | −7.85 | 11.12M |

Dropping warm-start was the only variant that raised token use, and it cost 11.12M against 8.41M.

QUOTES
- "information retained only in its interaction history disappears when the invocation ends." (p.6)
- "HoH adopts progressive disclosure rather than a dedicated memory module: plans, reports, histories and other artifacts are persisted in the filesystem and initially exposed through a concise, categorized index" (p.2)
- "Seventeen issues were reopened after an earlier closure when a subsequent change caused previously verified behavior to fail again." (p.15)
- "Every reported task–condition score is obtained from one valid run." (p.30)

LIMITS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW
- **Variance:** there is one run per cell, with no seeds or repeats. The bootstrap confidence intervals in Fig. 4 resample tasks only, not generations. Some individual tasks fall (OpenCode Autobattler −12.12, Pi Spire Descent −15.65).
- **No limitations section.** The paper only says future work will cover other software types.
- **Not a context test:** it never compares compaction against context reset, and never measures context-window behaviour. Each role is a fresh invocation, so "reset" is built in and unmeasured.
- **No entropy-management test.** It does not examine file or progress-file hygiene, and the 70-loop case has no baseline.
- **Case study is anecdotal.** It has no control and uses a different model from the benchmarks. A player-experience questionnaire (PXI) protocol is described in B.8, but no results appear in the extracted text.
- **FrontierSWE gains are narrow.** In the Codex per-task table (Table 17), 5 of 15 tasks score 0.00 at every HoH iteration, and the mean rise is carried by a few tasks (Granite Mamba2, Notebook Compression, Revideo).
- **Dominance is pool-dependent:** the same HoH@3 reads 71% in the 12-configuration pool and 39.33% in the 11-checkpoint pool.
- **Evaluation conditions:** the benchmarks are subsets. The QA stage is the same model as the developer, and the paper does not test that.
- **Token use:** Table 24 reports lower FrontierSWE tokens for HoH@3 than for Vanilla, which looks odd, and the paper does not explain it.
- **Dated model names** (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6-Sol, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MiniMax-M3).

BUILDS ON
- Larman and Basili, "Iterative and incremental developments", IEEE Computer 2003.
- Harness-optimization work: AutoHarness (Lou et al. 2026), Meta-Harness (Lee et al. 2026), and the harness survey (Li et al. 2026).
- Role-based multi-agent software workflows: MetaGPT (ICLR 2024), ChatDev, AgileCoder, EvoDev, and EvoMAC (ICLR 2025).

FIT FOR NOTE 06
Partial and weak-to-moderate. The cross-loop state split (artifact plus evidence), the progressive-disclosure index, and the warm-start ablation are relevant to state externalization and the session lifecycle. It does not address compaction against reset, progress-file design, or entropy. It fits better in note 07 (orchestration: Planner, Developer and QA roles, single-writer, independent QA) or note 08 (maturity). In 06, cite only the warm-start and evidence-feedback ablation, with its single-run caveat.

FIGURE CANDIDATE
Fig. 3 (p.5), the HoH overview: the three roles around an evolving artifact plus the evidence bundle. Fig. 1 (p.1), open and closed issues over the 70 loops, would also illustrate the lifecycle.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. The extraction was clean apart from garbled glyphs in equations.
